Marathon Petroleum stock ticked up just 0.28% today to close at $460.56, continuing a volatile week that saw it drop nearly 4% from Monday's peak before recovering slightly in the last two days. The modest gain fits with broader oil-market steadiness: Brent crude hit a fresh six-month high of $116 on escalating Middle East tensions—Trump accused Iran of manipulating oil prices, and U.S. diplomats are being pulled from Saudi Arabia as military action looms—yet those geopolitical fears appear to have largely priced in already, leaving little fresh catalyst for big moves today.

The real story for refiners like Marathon this week has been the underlying choppiness between threat and reality. Refinery utilization sits at a robust 93.4%, and the price spread between crude and refined products matters enormously to refiner margins—but with geopolitical risk already baked into oil prices and no major refining disruption materializing yet, the stock has settled after its sharp losses early in the week. The week's back-and-forth suggests traders are torn between betting on widening margins from high oil prices versus worrying that geopolitical shocks could quickly crimp demand or supply.
